diagrams.title: Runtime · engine integration
diagrams.question: Which engine contracts does one runtime session coordinate?
notes: GameRuntime borrows Context and AbstractGame for one session. Context owns compatible adapters and tracks its worker groups.
Audio and toolkit sessions have separate lifetimes; they are not implicit Context adapters.

diagrams.title: Display · engine integration
diagrams.question: Who consumes the live window and who consumes copied dimensions?
notes: Display owns its windows. Input and presentation borrow them; a resize payload does not extend their lifetime.
Native window calls belong on platform. Simulation and cameras use copied tick dimensions.

diagrams.title: Input · engine integration
diagrams.question: How do native polling, action contexts and tick consumers connect?
notes: Polling/direct binding changes run on platform; complete immutable observations cross into the tick.
Context attachments, capture and focus are separate contracts. A focus request does not enable record capture.

diagrams.title: Assets · engine integration
diagrams.question: How do loading, shared caches and drawable resources depend on each other?
notes: Preparation is CPU-only; upload/cache publication follows the provider owner and can publish entries incrementally.
Loader does not schedule worker jobs. Worker/dispatch wiring belongs in application composition.

diagrams.title: Resources · engine integration
diagrams.question: Who creates or retains graphics generations, and what implements their lifetime?
notes: Logical handles retain immutable generations. They do not keep a closed native graphics domain usable.
OpenGL retirement is collected on graphics; final handle release alone does not perform a GL deletion.

diagrams.title: Rendering · engine integration
diagrams.question: What does playback consume, and what prepares the immutable frame?
notes: Preparation resolves copied visual state. Playback consumes complete frames and retained resources rather than mutable game objects.
Arrows describe dependencies, not the chronological direction in which a frame is published.

diagrams.title: Text · engine integration
diagrams.question: Where do CPU font/layout work and graphics publication meet?
notes: Font lookup/layout/preparation are CPU stages. Upload follows graphics affinity; published frames can keep an older Generation.
Updater owns replacement scheduling and adoption. Toolkit authoring remains within each toolkit integration.

diagrams.title: GUI · engine integration
diagrams.question: How do the two toolkit modules connect input, fonts, uploads and retained passes?
notes: TGUI and RmlUi are alternatives with separate native authoring APIs; there is no common Engine widget/session manager.
Sessions mutate/record on UI or simulation. Uploaders publish on graphics; frames retain scenes without live widgets.

diagrams.title: Audio · engine integration
diagrams.question: What is the audio implementation, and how do explicit notification pumps reach engine owners?
notes: Audio is not a Context adapter. Playback runs on its own output clock, and output lifetime is separately owned.
Notification delivery uses explicit maintenance/pumping; attaching a runtime pump does not transfer ownership of output.

diagrams.title: Events · engine integration
diagrams.question: Which engine producers use the bus, and where are optional delivery services connected?
notes: The bus itself is immediate by default and includes no dispatcher or worker service. Delivery factories are explicit composition adapters.
Queued errors are owned by the registration error sink, not by a discarded dispatcher future.

diagrams.title: Dispatch · engine integration
diagrams.question: Which owners drain queues and which engine services retain producer endpoints?
notes: Runtime opens/drains/closes each queue on its selected owner. Submission endpoints retain queue state, not a borrowed facade.
Dispatch is owner-affine; it is not the general CPU pool. A detached batch can still be running when the queue is empty.

diagrams.title: Workers · engine integration
diagrams.question: How does shared physical capacity serve Context groups and internal consumers?
notes: Groups share physical worker capacity. Runtime simulation has its own owner; it is not a pool job.
General jobs can request platform work, but Pool itself has no graphics or dispatcher dependency.

diagrams.title: Memory · engine integration
diagrams.question: Which storage, construction and release contracts support engine caches?

evidence.via: CPU grid builder checks out managed byte backing

notes: Captured release contexts can outlive a facade. Storage bookkeeping and live object state remain distinct.
These are CPU contracts. They do not replace graphics-domain retirement or synchronize arbitrary object members.

diagrams.title: State · engine integration
diagrams.question: Which helpers are used by engine services, and which remain standalone alternatives?
notes: StateTracker and StateMachine are independent templates; isolated boxes here do not imply an engine-owned world/state model.
Singleton helpers describe existing service construction. They are not a recommendation to make application state global.

diagrams.title: Logging · engine integration
diagrams.question: How do subsystem writers reach named logging configuration and lifetime?
notes: Named categories share private backend state. Any asynchronous logging queue is separate from Workers::Pool.
Ordinary logging is separate from required exception/future propagation and bounded emergency reporting.

diagrams.title: Diagnostics · owner-specific observations
diagrams.question: Which engine owner produces each copied observation?
notes: There is no central diagnostics manager in this map: each snapshot follows its own owner and access rules.
Runtime statistics require synchronization with run completion. Counts and empty queues are not completion barriers.

diagrams.title: Utilities · engine consumers
diagrams.question: Where do local discovery, fit, numeric and placement helpers enter engine work?
notes: These are local values/functions, not one initialized engine service. No std or primitive dependency boxes are needed.
Time::DeltaTime measures local elapsed time; runtime simulation keeps its own selected tick-time policy.

diagrams.title: Runtime · application composition
diagrams.question: What does an application create, implement and retain for one session?
notes: The composition role owns Context, the game and GameRuntime. The game supplies init/update/frame/quiesce/deinit hooks.
Use the supplied compatible factory for the normal native/OpenGL assembly; manual adapters are shown in the focused composition view.

diagrams.title: Display · application access
diagrams.question: What is safe from platform hooks, and what should update read instead?
notes: Direct window and monitor operations require the platform owner; cross-owner requests use a saved platform endpoint.
Use copied tick dimensions for simulation layout. Monitor content scale and framebuffer pixels are distinct observations.

diagrams.title: Input · application actions and controllers
diagrams.question: What must initialization bind, and what does each update consume?
notes: Direct binding changes run during platform initialization. Reusable controllers retain a context endpoint and their own lease.
Updates consume semantic actions and copied observations; text input/focus is a separate focused view.

diagrams.title: Assets · application loading and playback
diagrams.question: Which values does a game load once, share and advance independently?
notes: Shared asset metadata stays immutable; application objects own transforms, gameplay and playback state.
A failed upload may leave earlier successful entries published. Validate looked-up handles and release game copies before backend closure.

diagrams.title: Resources · application uploads and retained draws
diagrams.question: What must an upload owner supply, and what do later draws retain?
notes: Decode may run on CPU workers; native upload must use the initialized provider/loading owner.
Ordinary sprite/text/UI loading supplies default materials. Direct pipeline/material construction is an advanced option, not a prerequisite.

diagrams.title: Rendering · application frame preparation
diagrams.question: Which real API types does one ordinary sprite draw touch?
notes: Advance camera/gameplay/animation in update. Preparation may be skipped; it only snapshots the chosen appearance.
Writers borrow one runtime slot for the hook. Native draw/upload work belongs to graphics; loaded assets already supply ordinary materials.

diagrams.title: Text · application font and label choices
diagrams.question: What is the normal path for a static label or a changing label?
notes: Static labels explicitly layout, prepare and upload after graphics initialization. Changing labels can use Updater instead of application futures.
Context supplies an embedded default font. Configure named families/defaults before consumers; changing the catalogue does not rebind existing handles.

diagrams.title: GUI · application-owned sessions and publication
diagrams.question: What does application code own when it selects a toolkit?
notes: Dashed choices are alternatives: select a toolkit, do not infer a shared Engine widget API. Its widgets/documents remain application-owned.
Application code feeds the complete input batch, selects pointer delivery, requests focus and publishes recordings. Quiesce UI calls before session closure.

diagrams.title: Audio · application-owned playback and outcomes
diagrams.question: What remains application-owned around playback, notification pumping and shutdown?
notes: Output lifetime is independent of Context. Keep the source file available for streaming, and close output after its producers settle.
Dropping a Voice handle does not stop playback. maintain()/notification pumping is explicit and does not advance the audio clock.

diagrams.title: Events · application registration and delivery
diagrams.question: What must producers, listeners and cleanup retain or choose?
notes: Immediate callbacks run on the producer. Explicit delivery selects a different owner and requires an independent error sink.
Dropping Registration does not unregister. Invalidate and settle entered callbacks before destroying borrowed targets.

diagrams.title: Dispatch · application owner requests
diagrams.question: Which endpoint should a producer save, and which owner executes its work?
notes: Save copyable endpoints during initialization. Platform work receives Context; simulation requests drain at update boundaries.
Read retained futures only when ready. Never wait on the owner required to finish the request; endpoint lifetime does not extend borrowed captures.

diagrams.title: Workers · application CPU preparation
diagrams.question: What capacity does the host choose, and what does a preparation producer retain?
notes: The preparation role supplies its own owned job inputs and may post a graphics follow-up. That dependency belongs to the job, not Pool.
A group cap does not create more physical workers. Context closes its tracked groups; an injected pool can continue serving unrelated groups.

diagrams.title: Memory · application object storage
diagrams.question: What are the ordinary pooled path and the explicit-reservation alternative?
notes: Start with pooled retained handles. Reservations are for explicitly selected construction with an allocator that satisfies the release contract.
Final handles retain release state; this neither synchronizes object contents nor authorizes use of a destroyed pool facade.

diagrams.title: State · application state choices
diagrams.question: Which value/observation contract matches an application component?
notes: These are alternatives, not mandatory layers. Trackers/machines need caller synchronization; a versioned snapshot copies value and revision together.
Observers run on setter threads. Publication coalesces latest values and is not an event history or owner assignment.

diagrams.title: Logging · application configuration and writers
diagrams.question: What should happen before producers start and after they finish?
notes: Configure used categories before writers; stop/settle producers before flushing and closing. Keep file callback targets alive through final closure.
Runtime thresholds cannot restore stripped calls. Logging failure handling and required operation failures remain separate.

diagrams.title: Diagnostics · application observations
diagrams.question: What can a live observer inspect, and what requires runtime completion?
notes: Query GameRuntime::diagnostics() before run or after synchronizing with its return/throw, never as a live runtime sampler.
Other snapshots have owner-specific rules. Empty queues/counters do not prove completion, budgets or hardware behavior.

diagrams.title: Utilities · application-local helpers
diagrams.question: Which local values and functions can a tool or game use without a runtime service?
notes: File discovery can block and its results do not refresh automatically. Bit proxies and borrowed index views retain their own lifetime/synchronization rules.
Use tick.delta_seconds for game simulation; DeltaTime measures an independent local elapsed interval.

diagrams.title: Runtime · simple adapter assembly
diagrams.question: What does Context assemble before any game session starts?
notes: The supplied native/OpenGL factory creates a compatible assembly. These are contracts, not a requirement for five separate libraries.
Input may be owned or explicitly borrowed. Context and game must survive GameRuntime use and cleanup.

diagrams.title: Runtime · practical tick and frame boundary
diagrams.question: Which values cross simulation and rendering without exposing mutable game state?
notes: The game reads a copied tick and prepares a borrowed frame slot; the renderer consumes a completed immutable frame.
Sequential and concurrent execution use the same API boundary. Frame preparation may be skipped without skipping authoritative updates.

diagrams.title: Runtime · practical shutdown and observation
diagrams.question: How do ordinary requests, host decisions and retained outcomes fit around runtime?
notes: An ordinary request can be deferred/cancelled by the one host policy. stop()/failure bypass negotiation.
Retained lifecycle snapshots are safe observations; they do not keep the game, Context or native adapters alive.

diagrams.title: Input · simple gameplay actions
diagrams.question: What is the smallest useful binding-and-read map?
notes: Bind physical controls once on platform; update reads semantic button state from the tick.
Held-state movement and observed down-time are application policies. Keyboard positions do not provide localized text.

diagrams.title: Input · practical UI capture and focus
diagrams.question: Which separate contracts request records and decide their keyboard recipient?
notes: Capture requests Events/Text; a focus lease separately selects keyboard routing. Neither operation retroactively changes a captured batch.
Feed the full ordered batch once. Pointer selection stays application-owned and independent of keyboard focus.

diagrams.title: Assets · simple loading and lookup
diagrams.question: What does ordinary application loading need before drawing a sprite?
notes: On the platform loading owner, load_assets() prepares/uploads synchronously. Look up and validate the retained sprite before use.
Default materials are supplied by ordinary loading; a custom shader is not a prerequisite for this path.

diagrams.title: Assets · practical shared sprite, separate playback
diagrams.question: What can be shared while each application object advances its own cursor?
notes: A cursor retains immutable CPU clip metadata, not the asset GPU handles. Each object owns its cursor, position and behavior.
Advance during update; preparation copies the chosen cell/style into a packet. Tilesets provide the parallel retained-asset path.

diagrams.title: Rendering · simple prepared frame
diagrams.question: What is the small immutable structure playback actually sees?
notes: A pass owns resolved packets; each packet retains the exact resources required by later playback.
No live camera, animation cursor, application object or toolkit widget is needed to consume this frame.

diagrams.title: Rendering · practical one-sprite draw
diagrams.question: Which names appear in a normal prepare_render_frame() implementation?
notes: Copy camera matrices into a pass, resolve using pass semantics/parameters/constraints, then add the returned packet.
The loaded asset already retains its ordinary material. Writers and their borrowed views last for this hook only.

diagrams.title: Text · simple static label
diagrams.question: What are the explicit stages for a label that rarely changes?
notes: The dependency arrows are not a timeline. Invoke layout, prepare, then upload; retain the Generation for frame preparation.
The embedded default font needs no application font catalogue plumbing. Upload still requires initialized graphics.

diagrams.title: Text · practical changing label
diagrams.question: Which boundaries does Updater manage instead of application-owned futures?
notes: Updater prepares, uploads and adopts replacements while the application continues using the last successful Generation.
Report/retry failures according to game policy. Published frames can retain older matching text geometry and atlas generations.

diagrams.title: GUI · TGUI publication
diagrams.question: What is the retained UI path for TGUI alone?
notes: Author native widgets/documents, feed input and record on the UI/simulation owner. Upload owned recordings on graphics.
Context-aware sessions inherit Engine fonts. Select pointer delivery/focus explicitly; stop toolkit calls before closing the session.

diagrams.title: GUI · RmlUi publication
diagrams.question: What is the retained UI path for RmlUi alone?
notes: Author native widgets/documents, feed input and record on the UI/simulation owner. Upload owned recordings on graphics.
Context-aware sessions inherit Engine fonts. Select pointer delivery/focus explicitly; stop toolkit calls before closing the session.

diagrams.title: Events · simple immediate notification
diagrams.question: What must a synchronous producer/listener pair actually retain?
notes: The callback runs synchronously on the producer. Concurrent producers can overlap callbacks.
Explicitly unregister; dropping the registration identity does not remove it. Settle entered callbacks before releasing borrowed targets.

diagrams.title: Events · practical delivery choices
diagrams.question: What selects platform, simulation or a serial worker listener stream?
notes: Choose one optional transport per registration. The bus does not find a thread automatically.
Copies of one worker transport share a serial FIFO stream; different transports can run concurrently. Keep an independent error sink alive.

diagrams.title: Workers · simple Context-owned groups
diagrams.question: How does a preparation producer get shared CPU capacity through Context?
notes: Context creates tracked groups over its lazy owned pool or a supplied shared pool. One group is not one physical pool.
Physical capacity must permit the requested concurrency. Context shutdown settles its tracked work while platform dependencies can progress.

diagrams.title: Workers · practical pool shared by contexts
diagrams.question: What stays shared, and what closes independently?
notes: The repeated Context/Group boxes represent different instances of the same Engine types. Both contexts retain shared physical capacity.
Stopping context A closes/drains group A. It does not close unrelated group B or force the supplied pool to shut down.

diagrams.title: Subsystems · interactions
diagrams.question: How do the 17 documented responsibilities relate inside Cheryl Engine?
notes: Responsibilities are not CMake libraries or universal manager objects. Arrows select architectural dependencies; optional capabilities are explained by the detailed views.
Audio output remains separately owned. Asset worker scheduling belongs to application wiring; Events uses explicit delivery adapters.

diagrams.title: Subsystems · simple execution boundary
diagrams.question: What does runtime coordinate, and where does optional queued work enter?
notes: The dedicated simulation owner is separate from general worker capacity. Display/graphics remain on platform.
These are dependency arrows, not a schedule. The runtime/dispatch/worker pages define actual draining and shutdown order.

diagrams.title: Subsystems · simple content and presentation
diagrams.question: Which responsibilities meet when visual content becomes retained draws?
notes: Assets, Text and GUI supply separate preparation paths. Retained frames/resources let playback avoid live application and toolkit objects.
CPU preparation and graphics upload have distinct owners. No live widget tree crosses to the renderer.
